findings.detail: All 9 FR-ids from requirements_output (FR-001–FR-009) appear in generator_output's requirements[], each with its statement unchanged. Checked by set membership, not a count comparison.

Every boundary condition from nfr_spec_output's 9 per-FR tables (23 total rows across FR-001–FR-009) appears in the SAME FR's nfrs[] in generator_output — no row dropped, none attached to the wrong FR.
All 4 assumptions tag real FR-ids (FR-001/FR-006, FR-001/FR-003/FR-004, FR-002, FR-007) and each is grounded in a vision.md roadmap/regulatory item or the FR's own workflow, not an untethered claim.

All 5 constraints map to a real regulatory_posture constraint_id (CON-01 Red, CON-02 Amber, CON-03 Amber, plus the Phase-3 roadmap scoping and the Green data-protection item) and each names the FR(s) it constrains.
All 3 risks map to a real open_risks id (OR-01, OR-02, OR-03) — OR-03 is correctly tagged program-level since it doesn't map to any single FR, not forced onto one.
No metrics field or claim appears anywhere in items; north_star_metrics (NSM-01, NSM-02) are referenced only via FR-008/FR-009's own traces_to, never copied into a third place.
compound_splits[0] matches requirements_output's own entry verbatim (split_into: FR-007, FR-005) — not re-derived, not dropped.
Both coverage_gap open_questions (offboarding/suspension, dispute handling) point at real lifecycle states absent from all 9 FRs — not invented for their own sake.
